recommendation: Keep the commit. It completes the seed issue in current build scope while preserving the already-correct security-page narrative. The duplicate FHIR-13828 needs no independent source change.
issue_request: FHIR-13827 was Published and resolved Persuasive with Modification. It asked for stronger guidance than a blanket "SHOULD use CORS" or permissive Access-Control-Allow-Origin approach for Internet-facing FHIR APIs.
initial_application: The issue was applied historically as GF#13827 in commit 9071f6d0d1, which softened source/security.html CORS wording and added W3C, Enable-CORS, and Moesif references. Later cleanup in 3baee24231 corrected spelling and modal wording, and current source/security.html:220-223 contains the intended conditional guidance.
additional_context: FHIR-13828 is a duplicate. FHIR-16428 and FHIR-17307 are the same CORS/http/security change family. During parallel source review, the active CapabilityStatement resource still had a CORS comment recommending Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and saying all servers SHOULD support CORS, which preserved the issue's ambiguity in generated conformance definitions.
reconciliation: Updated source/capabilitystatement/structuredefinition-CapabilityStatement.xml so CapabilityStatement.rest.security.cors no longer promotes permissive wildcard headers or blanket all-server CORS support. The comment now says CORS is appropriate when a server chooses to support browser-based JavaScript clients and should be configured according to security policy.
source_changes: source/capabilitystatement/structuredefinition-CapabilityStatement.xml: updated CapabilityStatement.rest.security.cors comment to remove Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and blanket all-server SHOULD guidance.
